https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cz7d.text: Image source, Ukraine state emergency service DSNS Image caption, Garages ablaze in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district after the latest Russian strike By Harry Sekulich Â and Â Dan Johnson ,Â Ukraine correspondent Published 8 August 2026, 05:23 BST Updated 30 minutes ago At least three people, including a child, have been killed in overnight Russian attacks near the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, a local official said. In the early hours of Saturday missiles hit east of the capital and witnesses reported hearing powerful explosions just days after strikes across Ukraine killed 21 people. The ballistic missile strikes killed three and wounded another three, the head of the regional military administration Timur Tkachenko said, adding that falling debris damaged apartment buildings and cars, while a fire broke out at a separate building. Emergency crews were also fighting fires at a building and fuel tank in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaly Klitchko wrote on Telegram. Ukraine's state emergency service DSNS shared photos showing garages, a business and a building on fire in Kyiv, adding: "The number of victims is being clarified." President Volodymyr Zelensky has arrived in the Serbian capital Belgrade for his first visit. He is due to meet with Serbian President Aleksandar VuÄiÄ to discuss economic ties, security issues and relations with the European Union. Zelensky is trying to build wider support for Ukraine, but VuÄiÄ has refused to apply sanctions to Russia. Serbia is trying to join the EU and has provided aid to Ukraine and promised to help it rebuild after the war. Earlier in the week, Zelensky said delays in receiving anti-ballistic systems from partners leads to "horrific casualties and destruction", saying that having a stronger interceptor capability "could have saved lives" in recent deadly assaults. The president later said the supply of interceptors from allies had been "significantly reduced" this year. It came after Ukraine hit two oil refineries deep inside Russia along with Moscow-linked vessels in the Black Sea, which Zelensky said was intended to limit oil revenues used by Russia to "finance" its war in Ukraine. Recent mediation talks have faltered, leading to an escalation of attacks between both sides. Mr. Katae Takashi. The discussions focused on financial market stability, sustainable finance, the exchange of institutional expertise and the potential for expanding cooperation in support of investment projects involving Japanese companies operating or interested in the Romanian market. In a post published on his LinkedIn page following the meeting, ASF President Alexandru Petrescu emphasized the importance of the dialogue: “I had the pleasure of meeting today, at the headquarters of the Financial Supervisory Authority, with H.E. Mr. Katae Takashi, Ambassador of Japan to Romania. During our discussion, we addressed topics regarding the balance of financial markets, sustainable financing, as well as the relevance of the exchange of good practices between authorities and institutions with responsibilities in the financial field. Japan’s experience in the development of financial markets provides valuable benchmarks, including in terms of stimulating interest in the capital market and the professional training of specialists. In this context, we discussed capitalizing on the bilateral dialogue through exchanges of experience and cooperation initiatives as applied as possible. We also analyzed the opportunity of mechanisms through which the capital market can support the financing of projects of Japanese companies present or interested in the Romanian economy. The interest shown in the Romanian market creates important premises for strengthening collaboration in areas relevant to non-banking financial markets. The meeting was an important opportunity for institutional dialogue and reconfirmed the openness to mutual support, exchange of expertise and the development of joint initiatives relevant to non-bank financial markets.” The meeting reflects Romania’s continued efforts to strengthen its financial sector through international partnerships and the exchange of best practices. Japan, one of the world’s leading financial centres, has extensive experience in capital market development, financial education and sustainable investment, areas that are increasingly relevant to Romania’s long-term economic agenda.” The talks also highlighted the role that capital markets can play in supporting Japanese investment projects in Romania. Enhanced cooperation between the ASF and Japanese financial institutions could facilitate greater investor confidence, improve access to financing and contribute to the further development of Romania’s non-banking financial sector. The meeting is another indication of the steadily expanding Romanian-Japanese partnership, which has gained momentum in recent years across economic, financial and institutional cooperation. 02.07.2026 Follow Nine O’Clock on social media via : LinkedIn, Facebook , and Instagram. https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026.text: Nathan Cofnas said in a post on X he was grateful to Ghent’s rector ‘for allowing me to stay’. Photograph: Adam Gerrard/Mirrorpix View image in fullscreen Nathan Cofnas said in a post on X he was grateful to Ghent’s rector ‘for allowing me to stay’. Photograph: Adam Gerrard/Mirrorpix Jason Arday Jason Arday accuser given three-month teaching ban but can continue research Nathan Cofnas allowed to resume Ghent University work, as US ambassador claims credit for lifting of suspension Chris Osuh Sun 30 Aug 2026 11.35 EDT Last modified on Sun 30 Aug 2026 11.50 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Prof Jason Arday’s accuser Nathan Cofnas has been barred from teaching on Ghent University campus for three months but has been allowed to continue his research position. Earlier this month Cofnas, an American academic, was suspended from his postdoctoral research position at the Belgian institution pending a “preliminary investigation” launched after Arday’s death. Ghent did not name Cofnas but has since confirmed it has “imposed a disciplinary measure” on a staff member for three months, under which they were “required to work remotely and may not carry out any teaching”. Cofnas’s research activities in the role have been “strictly limited to the research topics for which the appointment was made”. In a post on X, Cofnas said he was grateful to Ghent’s rector, Petra De Sutter, “for allowing me to stay”. The US ambassador to Belgium , Bill White, who had criticised Cofnas’s suspension, claimed on his official X account that the university and Cofnas had “amicably reached an agreement” to lift the suspension, enabling the academic to complete his one-year appointment. In a statement, Ghent said an inquiry was under way “to determine if further disciplinary action is warranted”. The university later confirmed it had been in contact with the US ambassador, who “provided further context regarding his statements on X”. Cofnas’s role at Ghent has been mired in controversy. In May, Ghent’s philosophy department alleged to university leaders that Cofnas had “very limited expertise” for his role researching “the future of liberalism”, alleging he had a “far-right agenda”. In July Cofnas accused Arday, a Cambridge sociologist, of plagiarism, alleging there were “serious questions” about his biographical claims. Arday was found dead on 14 August. His family paid tribute to him as an “amazing father, partner, brother, uncle and son”. View image in fullscreen Jason Arday was found dead on 14 August. He was accused of plagiarism by Cofnas. Photograph: Graeme Robertson/The Guardian White, a Donald Trump supporter, donor and fundraiser , had called Cofnas’s suspension “truly unacceptable”, calling for De Sutter to immediately rescind it earlier this month. On Friday, White wrote on his personal X account: “I just saved Belgium from a complete global media meltdown and well deserved spanking by @elonmusk and everyone by resolving the UGHENT Cofnas matter – quite quickly.” The night before, Cofnas thanked White and the US state department for “defending American values” on X, adding: “It was beyond my imagination that such a person would take an interest in the fate of a postdoc. The Ambassador responded with great support which helped to bring about a just outcome.” “Anti-woke” Cofnas has been accused of promoting pseudoscientific ideas of racial difference in his online writings, and was reportedly among bloggers recommended to the Palantir founder, Peter Thiel , by a “race science” researcher. Cofnas has also hit out at Trump and Maga in his writing, while claiming the US president’s executive orders against diversity, equity and inclusion in the US were a “cause for celebration”. In a piece in April last year he said the Republican party had “degenerated into a low-IQ cult of personality”. Hitting out at Trump’s tariffs, he said the effect “will be to halt the American economic juggernaut, discredit the anti-woke movement, pave the way for a leftwing populist … (and) stop the right’s momentum in other countries”. In October, he wrote: “The right simply does not have the human capital to retake the institutions and run them effectively. The vast majority of intelligent, psychologically stable, and public-spirited Americans remain left and woke. The Trump administration’s war on universities, science, and data has only reinforced smart people’s identity as leftists.” Asked by the Guardian if he stood by previous criticisms of Trump and Maga, Cofnas said: “I voted for Trump three times and I am still a registered Republican. I strongly criticised some Maga policies, particularly tariffs. There are other Maga policies that I support, such as interventions on behalf of free speech.” Ghent University said it did “not wish to comment further on the controversy surrounding this matter … ongoing preliminary disciplinary inquiries must be allowed to proceed calmly, independently and with full respect for the rights of all those involved”.
